body:
Today's scan found zero arbitrage opportunities across all 89 live contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket — a quiet day, not a broken scanner. That absence is worth noting on its own: even though several Kalshi settle above strikes and Polymarket touch low strikes bracket similar price levels, the underlying resolution rules differ enough (one pays out on a single settlement snapshot, the other on whether spot ever touches a level during the window) that the numbers don't line up into a clean, fee-adjusted edge.

The wide dispersion in strikes reflects genuine volatility in gold itself recently. Spot XAU/USD has swung hard over the past month, rising nearly 14% in a three-week rally to its highest level since mid-May near $4,700 before correcting lower, and more recently testing support around $4,300, down roughly 3.25% on the week (FXStreet). That round trip explains why Kalshi's Sept 30, 2026 and year-end ladders span everything from $3,570 to $5,500 with real pricing at each rung, and why Polymarket's September touch-low contracts at $4,000–$4,400 are trading at meaningful (not throwaway) probabilities.

Mechanically, most of the book looks thin: many far-out-of-the-money Kalshi strikes (e.g., the $4,690.99, $4,850.99, and $4,930.99 above contracts) show zero 24-hour volume, and Polymarket's $3,800 and $3,900 touch-low contracts trade under $100 in daily volume. Wide bid-ask gaps in that illiquid territory are a function of empty order books, not mispricing — worth keeping in mind before reading any single quote as a signal. Nothing today rises to the level of an unusual spread or a headline-driven dislocation warranting further digging.
headline: Zero arbitrage across 89 gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket as thin books track a volatile month
